messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Canary metric: median p95 latency jumped x5 for /v2/generate during rollout 2026-03-17T02:18Z. Canary group A failing. Paging oncall.
pagerduty: Paging dmitri (oncall) — urgent.
dmitri: taking this. first look now. what's the deploy tag?
sara: rollout tag = release/2026-03-17-v2. commit 9f3b2a. small change to batching logic.
leo: triage checklist: check canary percentage, traffic split, and feature flag state.
dmitri: running quick dashboard checks. aggregating metrics.
dmitri: confirmed p95 spiked from 120ms -> 650ms on canary nodes, errors ≈ 0.2% (5xx slightly up).
hana: rolling canary is 10% traffic. flag 'v2_dynamic_batch' enabled in canary.
ash: (note) saw similar regressions in local perf test for long-seq workloads earlier this week but flagged as non-blocking.
ash: sorry, meant mike — typo.
mike: i can reproduce a latency bump with large prompt in staging when kv-cache prefetch is enabled.
dmitri: ok kill switch time. hana — can you flip feature flag for canary only? want to isolate.
hana: on it. /redwoodctl feature toggle v2_dynamic_batch --env=canary --off
hana: done. canary traffic now using fallback batching.
nash: (ops) observing real-time: p95 dropping in 2 minutes.
dmitri: p95 back to 150ms, errors trending down. we should avoid full rollback; prefer targeted patch or revert single commit.
nash: we need a quick root cause. if commit 9f3b2a changed batching heuristics, can we bisect to minimal change?
mike: starting bisect: revert candidate lines in the batching module locally, running microbench harness.
nash: heads-up: customer-facing incidents? cs-bot: Customer Impact: 12 sessions affected (momentary latency) across two enterprise accounts; no errors in model outputs.
nash: good that errors were low. notify CS that we're on it and will update in 30m if stable.
nash: @ashley can you draft a short note?
nash: ashley: on it. brief: We saw a short latency spike during a canary rollout. Root cause suspected to be new batching heuristic. We disabled the heuristic for canary and saw metrics recover. Working on a quick patch and will follow up.
dmitri: bisect result — single line change in commit 9f3b2a that changed threshold from 64->128 triggers too-large batch formation for long sequences. Removing that change fixes perf in our microbench.
mike: i can prepare a minimal revert patch (single hunks) and open a hotfix PR.
dmitri: prefer single-commit revert and canary redeploy to confirm. hana — can you prepare to roll canary to 0 and then back to 10% after patch?
hana: yes. steps: 1) disable canary traffic 2) apply patch 3) rollout canary -> 10% 4) monitor 5) promote.
nash: also add a temporary safety gate: auto-fallback if p95 > 300ms for >2mins.
hana: implemented fallback policy in routing.
nash: mike: paste the revert command in thread.
mike: patch PR created: GH #4027. revert diff is one hunk. deploy command:
```bash
git checkout -b hotfix/revert-batching-9f3b2a
git revert --no-commit 9f3b2a
# verify tests
git commit -m "hotfix: revert batching threshold change (9f3b2a)"
kubectl apply -f deploy/canary-deployment.yaml
```
hana: canary disabled, applying patch now.
hana: patch applied, redeploying canary.
incident-bot: deploy started: canary release/2026-03-17-v2-hotfix-4027 at 2026-03-17T02:42Z
leo: metrics update: p95 back to baseline 130ms within 3mins.
dmitri: verified 5xx stable. scaling behavior normal.
sara: good — gradual promotion to 50%?
dmitri: keep at 10% for 10 more mins, then promote if stable.
nash: CS update: notifying impacted accounts now.
cs-bot: Message queued to customer contacts: "We've mitigated a short latency spike during a canary rollout by reverting a batching threshold change. No customer data or outputs were affected. We're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem."
nash: handing off to hana for watch and for postmortem doc. dmitri remains on-call until end of shift.
hana: ack. i'll watch metrics and collect flamegraphs. starting incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/4440001112 (draft)
dmitri: leaving a note to run extended load overnight on dedicated hardware.
nash: thumbs up. preliminary incident severity: Sev2 (short customer impact, quick mitigation). follow-up: postmortem in 48h, include regression tests for long-seq batching.
nash: thanks team. closing oncall page once canary promoted and stable for 30m.
leo: :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident update: canary at 10% stable for 12m, metrics nominal.
hana: final: promoted to 100% at 02:58Z, monitoring 30m. all good so far.
dmitri: back to normal ops.
nash: we should also add a perf regression gate to PR checks for batching heuristics.
nash: will own follow-up.
nash: closing thread in 1h after final verification. thanks everyone for fast response.
